Hi Jane —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side based on the questions your security team raised during the demo: 

- SOC 2: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report. I've attached a one-page SOC2-summary.pdf that highlights scope and controls. We can provide the full report under an NDA if needed.

- Encryption in transit & at rest: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we use AES-256. We support envelope encryption for model serving and persistent storage.

- Key management options: 
  - Hosted (default): Redwood manages keys (protected in our KMS) and we apply envelope encryption for customer data.
  - Customer-managed keys (BYOK): We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault where the customer retains root key ownership. Keys are used for wrapping/unwrapping and never stored in plaintext in our environment.
  - HSM-backed keys / private deployment: For customers requiring HSM-only key material and attestation, our Private deployment integrates with customer HSMs or vendor HSMs through a VPC and KMS proxy.

- Key rotation & access controls: We support automated rotation policies and audit logging; rotation can be coordinated with your KMS policies. Detailed operational controls are in the attached redwood-kms-options.pdf.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Please share your vendor security questionnaire (if you have one) — I can start filling it and loop in Marissa for technical answers.
2) Marissa (security), Neha (solutions) and I can set up a 30-min security deep dive next week to cover HSM attestation and data residency/GDPR concerns.
3) If you want the SOC 2 report under NDA, let me know and I'll initiate the NDA + secure share.

Thanks Jane — looping in Marissa (Security) and Neha (Solutions) to address the technical parts below. Reply inline where helpful.

> 1) For BYOK / customer-managed keys: can you confirm that the root key material never leaves our KMS (i.e., keys are never exported to Redwood)?

Camila (internal): Short answer: yes. For our BYOK flow we use envelope encryption. The customer root key stays in their cloud KMS (or HSM) and is used to wrap/unwarp data encryption keys (DEKs). Redwood does not persist the unwrapped key material. We can include a short diagram in the questionnaire to show the flow.

> 2) For the HSM scenario: do you support FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs and can you provide attestation/certificates?

Marissa (internal): We support FIPS-validated HSMs in our Private deployment and via partner HSM integrations. We can share vendor attestation/certificates under NDA. Will provide the HSM vendor list and validation docs during the call.

> 3) Key rotation: what is the procedure for emergency rotation and how do you ensure availability during rotation?

Neha (internal): Our rotation model uses versioned DEKs with seamless rollover. During rotation we keep previous DEKs for read/decrypt operations for a configurable retention window while issuing new DEKs for encrypt. We log rotation events and provide audit trails. In emergency rotation we coordinate with the customer's KMS admin to revoke/replace wrapping keys and we run a coordinated rewrap. We'll add the exact runbook steps to the questionnaire response.

> 4) Data residency / GDPR & HIPAA: do you offer regional deployment or data residency guarantees for production data?

Camila: Yes — for customers with residency requirements we offer region pinned deployments and Private deployment options that isolate data within the customer's VPC/region. We also have GDPR-facing data processing addenda and can support HIPAA BAA for covered customers.
